This policy explains what personal information Brazos collects, why, who receives it, how long it is kept, and the choices you have. "Brazos", "we" and "us" mean the operator of the Brazos mobile app and the Brazos website.

—

The short version

  • Brazos collects what it needs to run a marketplace for local work: your account details, what you post, your messages, your payments, and a location for each job.
  • Other users see your name, your profile, and the jobs and reviews you post. They never see your phone number, and they see a job's exact address only if they are hired for it.
  • Brazos does not sell your personal information, shows no advertising, and does not track you across other companies' apps or websites.
  • You can delete your account in the app at any time (section 7).
01

Who this covers

This policy covers the Brazos mobile app and the Brazos website. Brazos is operated from the United States and intended for use there. Your information is processed in the United States and wherever our service providers operate.

02

What we collect

Account details

  • Your name, as you enter it.
  • Your phone number. If you sign in by phone, a one-time code is sent to it by text message.
  • Your email address, if you sign in with email.
  • Your password, if you sign in with email, stored only as a cryptographic hash by our authentication provider — Brazos never stores or sees your actual password.

Your name and profile photo are shown to other users. Your phone number is collected for sign-in, account identity, recovery, and safety (including preventing a banned user from re-registering). It is not displayed on your public profile.

Profile information

An optional short bio, your preferred language, and the job categories you select. If you offer work: the services and prices you list, a short note about your availability, and whether you are accepting work. These are shown on your public profile, together with figures Brazos calculates from your activity in the app: your rating and reviews, completion rate, on-time record and typical response time.

Location

Location is handled in two distinct ways, deliberately:

  • Approximate, and public. When a job is posted with a location, the app stores a neighborhood-level text label (for example "Flatbush, Brooklyn, NY"). This label is visible to anyone browsing that job. To find that label, the app sends your coordinates, or the place you type, to OpenStreetMap's Nominatim service, which returns the area's name.
  • Precise, and restricted. When you post a job you can give its service address, and if you use "use my location" the app also stores exact coordinates for that job. The coordinates are used only to place the job on the map's aggregated hotspot view and to measure how far away it is. The address and coordinates are stored separately from the job listing itself and are readable only by the job's Customer and its hired Worker, who keeps access to them as part of the job's record. They are never sent to people browsing jobs: the map's hotspot view shows counts per area, never individual pins, and a Worker browsing sees only a job's area and its distance.

When you look for jobs near you, the app sends your current position to our servers to find the jobs within your chosen distance. It is used to answer that search and is not saved.

If you turn on "New jobs nearby" notifications, the app stores one further coordinate: an approximate point for your own location, used solely to measure which new jobs fall inside your chosen radius. It is readable only by you and is never shown to other users.

You can decline location permission. Jobs can be posted with a typed location instead, and nearby-job notifications simply stay off.

Photos and videos

The app collects photos and short videos in these places, with different visibility:

  • Job photos and a short video, attached by a Customer when posting. Visible to anyone who can see that job.
  • Completion photos and videos, attached by a Worker when marking a job done. Shown in the app to the Customer and the Worker on that job.
  • Review photos, attached to a review. Visible wherever the review is shown.
  • Profile photos. Visible to other users.
  • Photos sent in a conversation. Kept in private storage and shown only to the people in that conversation.

Job, completion and review media and profile photos are currently stored in public storage buckets, which the app's access rules do not protect: someone outside the job who has, or finds, a file's link could open it; private storage for completion media is planned.

Photos and videos may show the inside of homes and personal property. Only post media you have permission to post, and do not share anything the Customer would not want shared.

Messages and job activity

Messages you send, including text and photos; bids; hire requests and counter-offers; reviews and ratings you give and receive; issue reports you file about a job, and what you write in them; the schedule of a job, including a repeating one; and the status history of your jobs, including a Worker's on-the-way, arrival and running-late updates.

Speaking to search or to dictate a job's title and description is turned into text on your device. The audio is not sent to Brazos.

Payments

Payments are processed by Stripe. Your card number is entered into Stripe's own payment form and never reaches Brazos. Brazos keeps a record of each payment — the amounts, the fees, and its state (held, released, refunded) — and the event records Stripe sends about it, which can include the name and ZIP code on the card and the card's brand and last four digits. The detail in those event records is removed after 90 days; the record that the event happened is kept.

Stripe's payment form runs inside the app and may collect information about your device that Stripe uses to prevent fraud, under Stripe's own privacy policy.

If you choose to save a card for faster hiring, Stripe stores it, not Brazos, and you can remove it at any time in Payment methods. If you are paid as a Worker, Stripe collects the details it needs to pay you (such as your identity and bank account) in its own onboarding; Brazos keeps only a reference to that payout account and whether it can receive money. When you set up payouts, the app asks for an email address and passes it to Stripe as the contact email for your payout account.

After a payment is released, Brazos emails a receipt to the Customer and the Worker, where the account has an email address.

Moderation data

Blocks and reports you make, including any description you write in a report and what the report is about (a job post, a profile, a review or a message). Reports are visible to Brazos administrators. Blocks are not disclosed to the person blocked. Brazos refuses posts, bids, profiles, service listings, reviews and messages that contain certain words it does not allow; the refused text is not stored.

Device, notification and diagnostic data

If you enable notifications, a push token identifying your device, plus your per-category notification preferences and any quiet hours you set. Push tokens are stored so that only you can read them, are switched off when you sign out, and are deleted with your account.

When the app crashes or hits an error, a crash report (what failed, and the device and app version) is sent to Sentry. It is identified by your account id only, and email addresses and phone numbers are stripped from it before it leaves your device. Sentry also receives basic performance and session measurements: that the app was opened, how long it took to start and to draw its screens, how long its network requests took, and whether a session ended in a crash. Those measurements include the web addresses the app requested, which for a neighborhood lookup can include the coordinates looked up.

When the app starts it asks Expo's update service whether a newer version of itself is available. That request carries the app's version and platform, not your account.

The website

The Brazos website sets no cookies, runs no analytics and loads no scripts from other companies. Like any website, its host receives your IP address and basic browser details when you open a page. If you email us, we receive your email address and what you write.

03

What we do not collect

  • Your full card number or bank login. Card details go to Stripe directly.
  • Government identification documents. (A Worker's identity check for payouts is done by Stripe, and Brazos does not receive the documents.)
  • Your device's contact list.
  • Background location. Location is read only while the app is open and you are using a feature that needs it.
  • An advertising identifier. Brazos shows no advertising.
04

How we use it

  • To operate the platform: show jobs, deliver messages, run bidding, and display profiles.
  • To take, hold, release and refund payments, pay Workers, and send receipts.
  • To place jobs on the aggregated map view and show how far away a job is.
  • To send notifications you have switched on.
  • To enforce safety and the Terms of Service: reviewing reports, applying blocks, refusing words Brazos does not allow, suspending accounts, and preventing a banned user from re-registering.
  • To fix problems, diagnose errors, and measure how well the app performs.
  • To answer you when you contact us, to meet legal obligations, and to establish or defend legal claims.

Brazos does not sell your personal information, does not share it for advertising, does not use it for third-party advertising, and does not track you across other companies' apps or websites.

05

Who it is shared with

  • Other users, as described above — what is public, what is limited to the parties on a job, and what is private is set out in section 2.
  • Service providers who run the platform for us, each only for its own job:
    • Supabase — hosting, database, sign-in, and file storage;
    • a text-message provider, working for our sign-in service — delivering sign-in codes to your phone number;
    • Expo — push notification delivery and app updates;
    • Apple — delivering notifications to your iPhone, drawing the map, and opening a job's address in Apple Maps when you ask for directions;
    • Stripe — payments, saved cards, and Worker payouts;
    • Resend — receipt emails;
    • OpenStreetMap Nominatim — naming the neighborhood for a location;
    • Sentry — crash reports and performance measurements;
    • Cloudflare — hosting the Brazos website.
  • Authorities and others, where the law requires it, or where we believe in good faith it is necessary to protect someone's safety, to investigate fraud or a breach of the Terms of Service, or to establish or defend legal claims.
  • A successor. If Brazos is merged, sold or reorganized, your information may pass to the new operator, which must keep honoring this policy until it tells you otherwise.
06

How long it is kept

  • Account data is kept while your account exists.
  • Job listings, a job's address, messages, bids, and reviews are kept while the account exists, because they form the shared history of a job between two people, and afterwards as section 7 describes. A review you left about someone else, and their rating, remain part of their record.
  • Payment records are kept as the record of what was charged, held, released and refunded. The detail in Stripe's event records is removed after 90 days.
  • Reports and moderation records are kept as long as needed for safety, and may outlive the reported account so that a banned user cannot simply re-register.
  • Banned phone numbers are retained specifically to enforce bans.
  • The record of which version of the Terms and of this policy you accepted, and when, is kept.
  • Push tokens are deactivated at sign-out and removed when your account is deleted. Your nearby-jobs point is kept until you replace it or delete your account.
07

Deleting your account

You can delete your account in the app: Profile → Account & safety → Delete account.

You cannot delete it while a job or a payment is still in progress; the app lists what is outstanding.

On deletion we deactivate your account, permanently delete your sign-in identity, and remove your name, photo, bio and contact details from your profile. Jobs you posted that nobody was hired for are closed, and bids and hire requests still waiting on an answer are withdrawn. Your notification settings, push tokens and listed services are deleted. Any card you saved is removed from Stripe before the account goes. A Worker's payout account stays open until every payment still owed to them has reached it, so nothing earned is lost with the account. Content tied to past jobs — the job and its address, photos, messages, reviews — and payment records may be retained, shown under "Deleted user", so other users' job records stay intact and for dispute or legal needs. Uploaded media files are not yet automatically removed from storage; email brazosmvp@gmail.com to ask for a file to be removed. Moderation records and the record of the documents you accepted are retained as described above.

Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.

08

Your choices and rights

  • Location: decline the permission, or type a location manually instead.
  • Notifications: switch any category off in the notification settings under Profile → Notifications, or turn them off entirely in your device settings.
  • Saved cards: save one only if you want to, and remove it in Payment methods.
  • Profile details: edit or clear your bio, photo, and categories whenever you want.
  • Other users: block anyone, and report what they post.

Depending on where you live, you may have the right to ask for a copy of your personal information, to have it corrected, or to have it deleted. To make a request, email brazosmvp@gmail.com from the email address on your account, or tell us the phone number on it. We may ask for more detail to confirm the request is yours. We do not treat you differently for making a request. If we decline a request, we tell you why, and you can reply to ask us to look again.

09

Security

Your information is sent over encrypted connections and stored with our hosting provider. Access rules in the database are designed to limit each user to the information they are entitled to see; section 2 says which files those rules do not yet cover. Passwords are hashed by our authentication provider. No system is perfectly secure, and we cannot guarantee against every possible breach. If a breach affects your personal information, we will tell you as the law requires.

10

Children

Brazos is not intended for anyone under 18, and we do not knowingly collect information from children. If we learn we have, we will delete it.

11

Changes

We may update this policy. When the substance changes, you will be asked to review and accept the new version before continuing to use the app.

12

Contact

Privacy questions: email brazosmvp@gmail.com. Brazos replies within 2 business days.
